Dismissal Hearings Committee In Re: Denise Bennett Recommendation to the President of the University of Idaho August 30, 2019 Introduction The Dismissal Hearings Committee (DHC}1 received a request from Provost John Wiencek (hereafter "Provost") on June 18, 2019 to initiate the dismissal hearing process for Professor Denise Bennett. Professor Bennett (hereafter "Professor'') timely requested a hearing before the DHC.2 A panel (hereafter "Panel") of university faculty members was established from the membership of the DHC to conduct the hearing, and statements and evidence were gathered from both parties over July and August. The hearing took place on August 26, 2019, in the Best Western Plus University Inn in Moscow. Professor Bennett was represented by counsel at the hearing, as was the Provost. The Idaho Office of the Attorney General supplied a Hearing Officer, Mr. Lincoln Strawhun, to conduct the hearing. The Panel consisted of David Pimentel (chair), Kristin Henrich, Aleksandra Hollingshead, Marla Kraut, and Mark Schwarzlander. The Panel understands its responsibility as one of considering all the evidence, and making a recommendation to President Scott Green, whether the Provost has proven, by clear and convincing evidence in the record as a whole, that adequate cause for termination or dismissal exists. FSH 3910 D. The Panel considered all the evidence presented by both parties, as well as the testimony of nine witnesses at the hearing itself (five called by the Professor, and four called by the Provost). Based on all of this evidence, the Panel finds that the Provost has met his burden of showing, by clear and convincing evidence, adequate cause for dismissal. Timeline of Relevant Events, substantiated by the evidence as found by the Panel • January 22nd o Professor Bennett sent an email entitled "A MANIFESTO FROM A PROFESSOR WHO IS BEYOND FURIOUS" (hereafter referred to as the "Manifesto") to a long list of UI administrators and College of Letters, Art, and Social Sciences faculty. In this message, which was laced with profanity, and most of which was in all capital letters, Professor Bennett vowed to "NEVER GO TO ANOTHER MEETING INVOLVING THE WORDS ASSESSMENT OR STRATEGIC PLAN" and to "NO LONGER SPEAK IN PERSON WITH OR RESPOND TO EMAILS/PHONE CALLS FROM, ANYONE ASSOCIATED WITH THE ADMINISTRATION OF UI, CLASS, OSP, OR OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE UNITS I HAVE YET TO 1 https://www.webpages.uidaho.edu/fsh/1640.html#1640.36 2 The Provost issued an earlier Statement of Particularity on March 4, 2019, and a hearing was scheduled for mid­ May. The Provost withdrew that Statement of Particularity shortly before the hearing, as is his right under FSH 3910 D-2(c). The Provost issued a new Statement of Particularity on June 13, 2019 covering the same subject matter. It is the second Statement of Particularity which is the subject of this proceeding. 1
